meta.title: Operation of UV-Visible Spectrophotometer in Pharmaceutical Analysis Laboratory

sections.purpose: To quantitatively determine the concentration of pharmaceutical compounds by measuring their absorbance of UV or visible radiation, for assay, purity testing, dissolution testing, and stability evaluation as per pharmacopeial methods.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Analysis laboratory for all spectrophotometric analyses including drug assay, identification by UV spectrum, colorimetric methods, and optical density measurements for dissolution profiles.
procedure: Switch on the UV-Vis spectrophotometer and allow a minimum 20–30 minute warm-up for deuterium and tungsten lamp stabilization.
Set the required wavelength: UV range (200–400 nm) for aromatic compounds; visible range (400–800 nm) for coloured solutions or after colour development.
Select measurement mode: Absorbance (A) for standard quantitative analysis; Transmittance (%T) if required by method.
Select the correct cuvette: Quartz cuvettes for UV range (below 340 nm); glass or disposable plastic cuvettes for visible range (above 340 nm).
Prepare the blank solution (solvent or reagent without analyte) and the standard/sample solutions as per the validated method.
Rinse the cuvette 2–3 times with the blank solution before filling for the blank reading.
Fill the cuvette 3/4 full with blank, wipe exterior with lens paper, and insert into the reference beam (or sample compartment for single-beam instruments); press 'Zero/Blank' to set baseline.
Replace blank with the standard solution, wipe exterior, and measure absorbance. Verify it matches the expected value.
Measure sample solutions in sequence; wipe exterior of cuvette before each reading.
Read the absorbance value when the display stabilizes.
Calculate concentration using Beer-Lambert Law: A = εcl, or use a calibration curve constructed from standard solutions.
Rinse cuvettes with distilled water after organic solvents; with 1% HNO₃ after metal-containing solutions; then 3× distilled water.
Scan the full UV spectrum (200–400 nm) for drug identity confirmation and λmax verification.
Record all wavelengths, absorbance values, dilution factors, and calculated results in the analytical record.
precautions: Allow full 20–30 minute warm-up — readings taken before lamp stabilization are inaccurate and drift continuously.
Use quartz cuvettes for all measurements below 340 nm — glass absorbs UV and gives erroneously high absorbance.
Keep absorbance in the linear range (0.1–1.0 AU) for Beer-Lambert law compliance — dilute samples as needed.
Clean cuvette exterior with lens paper only — fingerprints absorb UV and cause errors.
Re-blank the instrument after changing wavelengths significantly (> 50 nm shift).
Do not measure strongly coloured solutions without confirming the appropriate wavelength — measuring at the wrong wavelength gives no signal.
Calibrate wavelength accuracy regularly using holmium oxide filter or certified wavelength standards.
